title: Justice: What's the Right Thing to Do?
extent: 24 lectures in the public video archive
description: Murder and the trolley problem, markets, rights, taxation, inequality, citizenship. Sandel uses Socratic public discussion.
remarks: Free public videos. Harvard Online also offers a free audit track; course readings may not all be publicly downloadable.

title: Philosophy and the Science of Human Nature
description: Classical philosophy paired with psychology, behavioral economics, literature, and cognitive science. Includes flourishing and procrastination.
remarks: Every lecture has free video and a written transcript; many lecture pages include assignments and downloadable reading guides.

title: Death
description: What is a person? Is there a soul? Is death bad? Would immortality improve a life?
remarks: Every lecture offers full text transcripts and free video; the course homepage contains a full course reading list.

title: Introduction to Political Philosophy
description: Political authority, citizenship, constitutionalism and democracy through Plato, Aristotle, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau and Tocqueville.
remarks: Traditional texts, but accessible problem-driven lectures with complete open videos and course transcripts.

title: The Science of Well-Being
description: Evidence-based examination of happiness, misleading intuitions and behavior change. Psychology rather than academic philosophy.
remarks: The official Yale page links to free course videos on YouTube and a free no-certificate Coursera option. Not a traditional philosophy course.

title: A Romp Through Ethics for Complete Beginners
description: A friendly introduction to moral dilemmas, free will, virtue ethics, utilitarianism and deontological reasoning.
remarks: Individual Oxford episodes support download of both video and written transcript.

title: Critical Reasoning for Beginners
description: Recognizing arguments, validity, induction, and identifying bad reasoning in everyday public arguments.
remarks: Individual episodes offer downloadable video and transcript. Series page displays seven items, while the numbered course contains six lectures.

title: Philosophy of Love in the Western World
description: Philosophy of love and sexuality through Tristan and Isolde, Don Juan, Nietzsche and modern literature.
remarks: Only four seminar sessions were filmed specifically for OpenCourseWare. Full weekly reading calendar and course materials are public.

title: Philosophy of Film
description: How film creates meaning, emotion and appearance/reality: Hitchcock, Welles, Renoir and cinematic form.
remarks: Four specially recorded classes, complete film/reading schedule, and sample student writing. Readings require access to films and books.

title: Philosophy in Film and Other Media
description: A philosophical comparison of cinema and literature using Amélie, Vertigo, The Seventh Seal and other works.
remarks: Four recorded seminars, a full 12-session film and readings schedule, and exemplar assignments.

title: Feeling and Imagination in Art, Science, and Technology
description: How imagination, emotion and creativity interact across scientific practice, technological design and art.
remarks: Four specially recorded seminar sessions and sample student papers on human/machine creativity.

title: Minds and Machines
extent: 25 sets of PDF notes across 26 sessions
description: Mind-body theories, the Chinese Room, Turing test, functionalism, perception, consciousness, and free will.
remarks: Nearly every scheduled lecture has a downloadable slide-note PDF, plus full bibliography, assignments and syllabus. No complete video archive listed.

title: How to Make a Moral Agent
extent: Topic-by-topic course slides & detailed reading plan
description: Can AI make moral judgments, lie, experience welfare or deserve moral responsibility? Combines philosophical traditions and modern AI research.
remarks: Spring 2026 course page contains lecture slides (PDF/print links) and primary/secondary readings attached to dated lectures. No public video series verified.

title: God and the Good Life
instructor: Meghan Sullivan, Paul Blaschko and colleagues
extent: Digital essays, course calendar and readings
description: Philosophy as a way of life: morality, epistemology, religion, God, trust, happiness and human purpose.
remarks: Substantial online lesson texts, annotated readings and original media; no public complete lecture-video archive verified.

title: Philosophy of Mind (PHIL 132)
description: Searle on consciousness, intentionality, computation and the nature of mental states.
remarks: Hosted by an unofficial uploader (SocioPhilosophy), not a current official UC Berkeley course mirror; do not treat as a verified complete official archive.

title: The Science Fiction of Freedom
description: Philosophy of freedom with Gattaca, Ursula K. Le Guin, Philip K. Dick, Octavia Butler, Rawls, Sartre and Parfit.
remarks: Instructor explicitly says the 2024 lectures were not recorded. Strong week-by-week reading plan and assignments, not full lecture notes. Required texts per the OCW syllabus: Philip K. Dick's Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, Louise Erdrich's Future Home of the Living God, and Charles Yu's How to Live Safely in a Science Fictional Universe; OCW's Instructor Insights confirms 26 class sessions met (two per week), first offered Fall 2024.

title: Happiness (Gen Ed 1025)
description: Happiness through Stoicism, Epicureanism, Buddhism, Daoism, contemporary philosophy, psychology and economics.
remarks: Harvard DCE explicitly describes on-demand lecture recordings for enrolled students; no public free recording or full open reading list verified. Harvard's official syllabus host (SimpleSyllabus, PHIL E-155 companion sections) confirms the structure — 22 reading-quiz-covered lecture topics, two per week (Tue/Thu), plus midterm and final — but displays the full session schedule to registered students only (checked October 2026).

title: Sex, Love, and Friendship (PHIL 16)
extent: Course description, no public teaching archive
description: Philosophical questions about intimacy, sexuality, friendship, and obligations in relationships.
remarks: Official Harvard course catalogue confirms title, instructor and description. No freely accessible full videos or substantial lecture notes verified. No public session-by-session listing exists anywhere as of October 2026 — the catalogue PDF now redirects, and the department site and the instructor's website list the course by title only.
